entries.title: Same-type attack bonus (STAB)
entries.text: STAB is a damage bonus when a Pokémon uses a move that matches its own type. It rewards choosing attacks that fit the user. The exact multiplier can depend on the game's mechanics, abilities, and transformations.

entries.title: Physical and special attacks
entries.text: Physical moves use Attack and Defense; special moves use Special Attack and Special Defense. In Generations I–III, a damaging move's type determines its category. From Generation IV, each move has its own category. Status moves do not use these ordinary damage calculations.

entries.title: Effort values (EVs)
entries.text: Effort values are training values that affect a Pokémon's stats. Competitive sets often describe an EV spread to prioritize particular stats. Modern EV rules must not be applied unchanged to the original games: Generations I–II use stat experience, and some other titles have separate training systems.

entries.title: Individual values (IVs)
entries.text: Individual values help determine the stats of an individual Pokémon, so two Pokémon of the same species and level can have different stats. Generations I–II use DVs instead. The game matters when discussing ranges, inheritance, or ways to improve these values.

entries.title: Natures
entries.text: In games with natures, a nature can raise one non-HP stat and lower another, or leave all stats unchanged. Natures are absent in Generations I–II. A useful nature depends on the moves and role you want that Pokémon to have.

entries.title: Abilities
entries.text: An ability is a Pokémon's passive effect. Only abilities available to that species and form in the selected game should be recommended. Abilities are absent in Generations I–II and are not an active mechanic in every later title.

entries.title: Type coverage
entries.text: Offensive coverage describes the opposing types your moves can hit effectively. Defensive coverage describes weaknesses, resistances, and immunities across your team. Good type coverage helps, but speed, move power, abilities, utility, and the opponent's set also matter.

entries.title: Base stats and actual stats
entries.text: Base stats describe a species or form. Actual stats also depend on the individual Pokémon and game rules, including level and applicable training values. A higher base-stat total alone does not guarantee a better teammate.

entries.title: Held items
entries.text: A held item is carried by a Pokémon and can affect a battle or enable an evolution. Its effect is different from using an item from the bag. Original Red, Blue, and Yellow do not have held items.

entries.title: Competitive legality
entries.text: A legal team obeys one exact format's rules: allowed Pokémon, moves, abilities, items, and other restrictions. Smogon tiers and official regulations are different rulesets. Being legal in a simulator does not show where or when you can obtain that Pokémon during a story playthrough.
